name: Goa
tagline: Two coastlines in one state: party-bright north, palm-quiet south
hero_description: India's smallest state packs a double life: the buzzing water-sports beaches of Baga and Calangute in the north, and the slow, palm-fringed sands of the south. Between the two sits 450 years of Portuguese history — the UNESCO-listed churches of Old Goa and the painted lanes of Fontainhas — that most beach itineraries never see.
best_time_to_visit: November to February — dry days at 21–32°C with a calm, clear sea; January gives you peak-season weather without the December crowds. (Monsoon bonus: June–September is when Dudhsagar Falls runs at full force.)

top_attractions.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
top_attractions.description: Consecrated in 1605 and part of the UNESCO World Heritage churches of Old Goa, this laterite basilica holds the relics of St. Francis Xavier — the feast in his honour fills Old Goa every 3rd of December.

top_attractions.name: Dudhsagar Falls
top_attractions.description: A four-tiered, roughly 310-metre cascade on the Mandovi River inside Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary, reached by a bumpy shared-jeep safari from Kulem — at its thundering best during and just after the monsoon.

top_attractions.name: Fontainhas, Panaji
top_attractions.description: Goa's Portuguese-era Latin Quarter: narrow lanes of ochre-yellow, green and indigo houses with azulejo-tiled name plates, best explored on a slow morning walk with a bakery stop.

top_attractions.name: Fort Aguada
top_attractions.description: A 1612 Portuguese sea fort above Sinquerim Beach, built around freshwater springs that once resupplied passing ships — its four-storey lighthouse is among the oldest of its kind in Asia.

top_attractions.name: Baga & Calangute beach belt
top_attractions.description: The state's water-sports headquarters — parasailing, jet-ski and banana-boat rides off a near-continuous 7 km stretch of sand shared with Candolim.

top_attractions.name: Anjuna Flea Market
top_attractions.description: The Wednesday institution that has run since Goa's 1960s hippie days — stalls of spices, silver and handicrafts spread behind Anjuna's rocky beach.

activities: Parasailing, jet-ski and banana-boat rides at Baga–Calangute
Jeep safari to Dudhsagar Falls with a swim in the plunge pool (seasonal)
Heritage walk through the painted lanes of Fontainhas
Old Goa churches circuit — Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral
Sunset cruise on the Mandovi River from Panaji
Spice plantation tour in Ponda with a traditional Goan lunch
Beach-shack seafood crawl — fish recheado, chicken xacuti, bebinca
Night shopping at the Arpora Saturday Night Market
